title: Faithfulness of base change on power-torsion modules characterises faithful flatness of the quotient map
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring map R -> S and an ideal I of R, and establishes the equivalence of four conditions: that the map be flat with R/I -> S/IS faithfully flat; that the map be flat with Spec(S/IS) -> Spec(R/I) surjective; that the map be flat with base change faithful on modules annihilated by I; and that the map be flat with base change faithful on I-power torsion modules (source lines 24226-24239). The proof first notes that flatness of R -> S gives flatness of R/I^n -> S/I^nS for every n, so (1) and (2) are equivalent by the faithful flatness criterion (proof lines 24242-24245). The equivalence of (1) with (3) follows by identifying I-torsion R-modules with R/I-modules, using the identity M tensor_R S = M tensor_{R/I} S/IS for R-modules M annihilated by I, together with the easy faithful flatness lemma (proof lines 24246-24252). The implication (4) implies (3) is immediate. The substantive direction is (3) implies (4): assuming (3), the proof uses the previously established flatness of R/I^n -> S/I^nS and the induced surjection on spectra, which follows because Spec(R/I^n) = Spec(R/I) and similarly for S, to conclude that base change is faithful on modules annihilated by I^n; since an I-power torsion module is the union of the M_n annihilated by I^n, and tensor product commutes with colimits, faithfulness extends to all I-power torsion modules (proof lines 24253-24260). The non-routine content is the passage from bounded torsion to all power torsion via the colimit description.
